previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and multiple prior surgeries was admitted with a Crohn’s flare, abdominal pain, and facial swelling. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction but revealed chronic complete occlusion of the SVC and brachiocephalic veins with collateralization, explaining her neck swelling. She developed a suspected central line infection in her right internal jugular catheter, presenting with fever and erythema, and was treated with intravenous Vancomycin. Due to non-functional lines and venous thrombosis, she required multiple central line revisions, ultimately receiving a femoral tunneled line for outpatient antibiotic therapy, which dislodged before discharge. Her abdominal symptoms improved with bowel rest, NG decompression, and pain management. She was discharged home after nine days of antibiotics, afebrile, with improved pain control, and a plan for close outpatient follow-up, including blood work and monitoring for infection recurrence.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  A ___ woman with SVC syndrome, for assessment of patency
for bilateral internal jugular veins.

___.

LIMITED NECK ULTRASOUND:  Grayscale and color Doppler sonography was performed
of the bilateral internal jugular veins.  Both are compressable, and patent
without evidence of intraluminal thrombus.

IMPRESSION:  Patent bilateral internal jugular veins.

PREOP PA AND LATERAL CHEST ON ___:

HISTORY:  Superior vena cava syndrome.

IMPRESSION:  PA and lateral chest compared to ___:

Previous right jugular and central venous line, with errant placement, has
been withdrawn.  New peribronchial opacification in the right upper lobe
suggests bronchiectasis, rather than pneumonia.  Lungs are otherwise clear.  A
13 mm long section of tubing projecting over the left second rib anteriorly on
today's study and ___ is not identified with certainty on the
lateral view, but appears to be a retained catheter fragment in the soft
tissues of the anterior chest wall, as early as ___ PET/CT 2:1. 
At that time, there was no soft tissue reaction around the fragment, and if
there are no associated physical findings, it probably is clinically
insignificant.

INDICATION:  Chronic SVC syndrome, back pain after central line placement.

___.

FINDINGS:  There is no focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. Right
upper lobe peribronchial opacification is unchanged. Cardiac and mediastinal
silhouettes and hilar contours are normal.  The retained catheter fragment
projects over the left axilla.  

IMPRESSION:  No pneumothorax.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Central line placement.

Portable AP radiograph was reviewed in comparison to ___ obtained
earlier.

No central venous line was placed.  Current study demonstrates no evidence of
pneumothorax.  There is right upper lobe opacity that appears to be even more
pronounced than on the prior study.
Vascular stend projecting over left axilla is unchanged in appearence.

INDICATION:  ___ female with SVC syndrome.  Rule out pneumothorax.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior studies including most recent ___  ___

AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  There is no pneumothorax.  Right upper lobe
peribronchiol opacity is likely the residual of prior infection. Lungs are
elsewhere clear.  There is no appreciable pleural effusion.  Heart size is
normal.  Mediastinal silhouette, hilar contours and pulmonary vasculature are
normal. A cylindrical foreign body projecting over the left axilla has been
present for years.

IMPRESSION: No pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  History of Crohn's disease with bowel distension, assess for
obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  This is a limited study due to inadequate centering of radiograph
over the patient's abdomen.  Air is seen within the stomach as well as
throughout loops of either small bowel or colon.  There are no air-fluid
levels.  No free air is seen in the abdomen.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Cannot adequately evaluate the bowel gas pattern given the inadequate
positioning of this radiograph.

2.  No evidence of free air.

INDICATION:  SVC occlusion with abdominal pain and constipation, evaluate for
obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  There is gaseous distention of multiple loops of colon.  No

air on this single supine portable radiograph.

IMPRESSION:  Findings most consistent with ileus.
